paragraphs.title: Removing the Mark or Cleansing the Item

easy.question: What does the priest do if the mark becomes fainter after washing?
easy.explanation: If the mark becomes faint, the affected section is torn out.

easy.question: What is done if the mark appears again?
answers: The affected garment or leather item is burned
It is placed in the sun
easy.explanation: If the mark appears again, the item must be burned.

easy.question: What happens when the mark disappears after washing?
answers: It is washed a second time and becomes clean
easy.explanation: When the mark departs, the item is washed a second time and is clean.

medium.question: What does “somewhat dark” mean in “the plague be somewhat dark”?
answers: It has become weaker or less noticeable
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a mark that has faded or become less prominent.

medium.question: Why is the garment torn in one case but burned in another?
answers: The first garment is new and the second old
In the first case the mark faded; in the second it appeared again
The first concerns leather and the second only wool
medium.explanation: A faded mark is removed by tearing, while a returning mark requires burning the item.

The item is torn, the mark disappears, and then it is burned
The item is washed, the mark disappears, and then it is washed again and cleansed
medium.explanation: The item is washed, the mark departs, and a second washing makes it clean.

challenge.question: Why is the item burned only if the mark appears again?
answers: Its return shows that the problem remains
The first washing always cleanses it
The mark is merely external dirt
challenge.explanation: A returning mark shows that the problem was not truly removed.
